Senses.Explanation: Literally, to 'go along walking' or 'walk about.' The term occurs 1,022 times in 273 allowed texts and names an observable bodily action. A late biography makes the direction explicit: at night a recluse goes outside the crag to walk about, the visiting master follows, and 'each walks east and west' (隱者出巖外經行，師亦隨之，第東西各步). A Five Lamps address pairs physical condition and action: 'when well, walk about; when tired, rest' (健即經行困即歇). The same collection records Layman Feng Ji walking about the teaching hall with Foyan when a child recites a line, and records another monk 'walking under the pines one evening' when he hears a mountain spring (一夕，松下經行，聞巖泉聲). In the collected old cases, Sudhana searches in all four directions for seven days and finds Meghashri 'walking slowly on another peak' (在別峰上徐步經行). Daily timing is also explicit: a biography says a monk ate only after serving the assembly, while Bingseng watched him 'walk about after each meal' (每飯罷經行時). The term is frequently coordinated with sitting and lying as one of the body's recorded activities. These places, times, directions, companions, and contrasts support the plain action word.
Senses.Note: All required definition formulas were searched; no stable nominal self-definition was found. Distinct deployment shapes retained are walking east-west at night, walking when well versus resting when tired, walking with another person in a hall, walking under pines, slow walking on another peak, and walking after a meal. The entry adds no special category beyond what the people in the records physically do.

Occurrences.Kwic: 隱者出巖外經行，師亦隨之，第東西各步。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Preceptor Zhuanyu Heng at Purple Bamboo Grove (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄): in the biography of Hanshan Deqing, an unnamed hermit living in a rock shelter goes outside at night to walk; Hanshan follows and the two walk separately east and west. The line, expanded context, section header, book title, TEI header, and parallel-passage search do not give a personal name for the unnamed rock-hermit.

Occurrences.Kwic: 若也見得行得，健即經行困即歇。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): in Longya Zhicai's explicitly headed section, Longya Zhicai tells the assembly that if it sees and can carry it out, it should make the walking circuit when vigorous and rest when tired.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一日，同遠經行法堂，偶童子趨庭吟曰：萬象之中獨露身。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Feng Ji biography. Feng Ji is the biographical subject and exact grammatical actor who walks through the teaching hall together with Foyan Qingyuan when a child recites the line that prompts his breakthrough.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一夕，松下經行，聞巖泉聲，微有所觸。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): in Songyin Mao's explicitly headed biography, Songyin Mao makes the walking circuit beneath the pines one evening, hears the rock-spring, and is slightly touched by it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 德雲比丘四維尋覔七日方見在別峰上徐步經行
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Connected Anthology of Verses on Old Chan Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集): the anthology's named Sudhana episode makes Deyun Bhikshu the exact actor: after a seven-day search, Sudhana sees Deyun slowly making the walking circuit on another peak.

Occurrences.Kwic: 病僧每飯罷經行時，見子事眾畢方就飯堂
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Preceptor Zhuanyu Heng at Purple Bamboo Grove (紫竹林顓愚衡和尚語錄): referring to himself as the sick monk in his instruction to Wanbai Hao, Zhuanyu Guanheng recounts making the walking circuit after meals and observing Hao's consistently careful service and eating routine.
